rationale: AMGmk is a dense sparse-linear-algebra multigrid solver whose hot code is arithmetic-heavy loops (hypre_CSRMatrixMatvec, MatvecT, Matvec_FF, relax, GenerateSeqLaplacian), so passes with low execution overhead should dominate: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain weight since arithmetic substitution is nearly free at runtime and this benchmark is rich in integer/float ops to transform, while SPLIT and IGV also receive strong security/diversity weights because basic-block splitting and indirect global-variable access add static-analysis friction with minimal loop-body cost. FLA and BCF are deliberately suppressed (high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights, low SecurityGain weight) because flattening and bogus control flow inflate the branch-mispredict- and I-cache-sensitive inner loops of SpMV and relaxation and would bloat the already largest functions (hypre_CSRMatrixUnion, GenerateSeqLaplacian), keeping size overhead acceptable for a 16.5KB text footprint. IBR and ICALL sit in the middle: indirect branching/calls meaningfully raise reverse-engineering resistance on dispatch-like and cross-file call sites (45 functions across 12 files gives real inter-procedural diversity to exploit) but their indirect-branch and function-pointer costs and higher correctness risk (ICALL especially, given the codebase's memory-management and error-handling code in hypre_memory/hypre_error) warrant moderate weights and elevated CorrectnessRisk penalties so they are applied selectively only where function features strongly favor security gain.
